column3: The Hebrew repeats Shechem as the destination of all Israel; BSB uses “there.”
The Hebrew repeats Jeroboam’s name; BSB leaves the second occurrence implicit.
The Hebrew names Jeroboam as the one who came and leaves the person summoned implicit; BSB names him in the summons and then uses “he.”
The Hebrew calls the first yoke hard and the father’s service hard; BSB expresses the first as a heavy yoke and the second as the burden of service.
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB supplies Rehoboam.
The Hebrew describes the elders as standing before Solomon’s face; BSB renders this as serving him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves Rehoboam unnamed and describes the young men as standing before him; BSB names Rehoboam and says they served him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “my little one,” without an explicit noun for a body part; BSB supplies “finger.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they came “on the third day”; BSB begins “After three days.”
The Hebrew explicitly adds that the elders had advised him; BSB leaves that relative clause implicit.

The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and says the word was spoken “by the hand of Ahijah”; BSB uses “He” and “through Ahijah.”
The Hebrew says Israel went to its tents; BSB says the Israelites went home.
The Hebrew says “sons of Israel”; BSB uses “Israelites” and adds “still” to Rehoboam’s reigning.
The Hebrew separately relates the stoning and his death; BSB combines them as stoning him to death.

The Hebrew uses singular “the heart of this people”; BSB says “their hearts.”
The Hebrew uses a pronoun for the recipients of the king’s speech; BSB supplies “the people.”
The Hebrew says “the one” twice without explicitly naming a calf; BSB supplies “calf” and uses “the other” for the second.
The Hebrew says that they went before the one, without explicitly naming worship or calves; BSB supplies “to worship” and “of the calves.”
